title: Finite difference normal forms

based_on.title: How to approximate fuzzy sets: mind-changes and the Ershov Hierarchy
based_on.pages: Article55; The Classical Ershov Hierarchy, Definition3 and Theorem3; classical finite-level statements with expanded constructive proofs

summary: Represent a fixed finite revision allowance by a descending chain of enumerable sets, and recover an approximation by counting positive stage discoveries modulo two.
abstract: A membership guess that can change a fixed number of times can be described by finitely many positive discoveries. One list records the inputs that have reached their first revision, another records those that have reached their second, and so on. These lists are nested, and an input belongs to the final set exactly when it reaches an odd number of them. Conversely, finite enumerations of a nested chain give an approximation: add their current membership bits and take the parity. Every revision spends at least one new discovery, so a chain with a given finite number of sets permits at most that many revisions per input. The two constructions identify finite change classes with finite alternating differences of enumerable sets, including the empty family. A representation supplies an upper bound; it need not use the smallest possible number of revisions.
